_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the cross-language pinning corpus for the SQL canonicaliser (plan section 7.2, Layer 1). EDIT THIS FILE, not its copies. Derived from iznik-server-go/ormharness/canonical_test.go's actual assertCanonicalEqual/assertCanonicalNotEqual test cases - not independently invented - and consumed by BOTH a Go test (iznik-server-go/ormharness/canonical_corpus_test.go) and a PHPUnit test (iznik-batch/tests/Unit/OrmHarness/CanonicalTest.php) against their respective Canonical() implementations. This exists because two independently-maintained canonicalisers (Go for iznik-server-go, PHP for iznik-batch - PHP cannot import Go code, so the PHP side is a faithful line-by-line port, not a shared binary; see iznik-batch/tests/Support/OrmHarness/Canonical.php's own header for why literal binary-sharing was rejected as impractical) will drift the day someone fixes a bug or adds a keyword on only one side. This file is what turns that drift into a CI failure on both sides instead of a silent divergence nobody notices until a manifest's notion of 'equal SQL' stops matching the other's. TWO BYTE-IDENTICAL COPIES exist, one inside each service's own tree (iznik-server-go/ormharness/canonical-corpus.json, iznik-batch/tests/Support/OrmHarness/canonical-corpus.json) - discovered necessary, not chosen for convenience: both test runners' containers are isolated to their own service subtree (the Go apiv2 image's build context is iznik-server-go alone; the Laravel batch container only bind-mounts iznik-batch), so neither can read this file directly at test time, and go:embed cannot reach outside its own module tree either. tools/orm-migration/check-canonical-corpus-sync.sh (wired into gate (q) in ci-ratchet.sh) fails the build if any copy drifts from this one. After editing this file: cp it over both copies, or run the sync-check script to see the exact commands. If you change either Canonical() implementation, add or update a case here (and re-sync the copies) so both languages' tests see it - a change that only updates one language's own test suite has NOT actually proven the two still agree.
